chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
Buying a first property in Quebec when you've just arrived comes with particular challenges: building local credit, understanding a different system, and navigating vocabulary and rules specific to the province. With the right support, it's entirely achievable.

This guide provides newcomers with reference points: credit and financing, Quebec particularities, and steps to get prepared.

Informational content. Each chapter ends with a lined “My Notes” page.

chapters.title: Building Your Credit and Financing File
chapters.objective: Becoming financeable within the local system.
chapters.html:
Becoming financeable within the local system.

Lenders look at your Canadian credit, your income, and your stability. A local credit history can take time to build; some programs exist for newcomers, with special conditions.

  • Start building credit early (a card, on-time payments).
  • Gather proof of income and employment.
  • Explore newcomer programs with a mortgage broker.
Émilie's tip

Start building your Canadian credit as soon as you arrive, even modestly: it's the key to getting good financing later. A mortgage broker knows the programs suited to newcomers.

chapters.title: Understanding Quebec's Particularities
chapters.objective: Learning the local rules of the game.
chapters.html:
Learning the local rules of the game.

  • The role of the notary (mandatory) and the real estate broker (regulated by the OACIQ).
  • The Welcome Tax, and municipal and school taxes.
  • Divided/undivided co-ownership, leases, and rental rules if it's a plex.
  • Particularities of the building stock (clay soils, French drain, heating, winter).

These elements often differ from what exists elsewhere: understanding them avoids many surprises.

Émilie's tip

Don't assume the system works “the same as in your home country.” Ask lots of questions: a good broker and a notary take the time to explain each step to newcomers.

chapters.title: Getting Prepared and Surrounding Yourself Well
chapters.html:
Moving forward with confidence.

Like any first-time buyer, prepare your budget, get a pre-approval, and define your criteria and target areas. As a bonus, surround yourself with professionals who understand your journey and can guide you (a broker, a mortgage broker, a notary).

Taking the time to learn the local market before buying is an investment that pays off.

Émilie's tip

Surround yourself with patient professionals who take the time to explain things plainly. Buying within a system you're just discovering is perfectly doable — with the right people around you.

chapters.title: Action Plan
chapters.html:
Your next steps, in concrete terms.

This week

  1. Start or build up my Canadian credit.
  2. Gather my proof of income and employment.

Within 30 days

  1. Meet with a mortgage broker (newcomer programs).
  2. Learn about Quebec's particularities.

After that

  1. Get a pre-approval and start my search with Émilie.

chapters.title: Resources & Glossary
chapters.html:
• Canadian credit: a local history, the key to financing.
  • Newcomer programs: adapted loan conditions, through a broker.
  • OACIQ: the body that regulates real estate brokers.
  • Welcome Tax: municipal transfer duties.
  • Pre-approval: an amount and rate confirmed before you shop.
